name: South Carolina

code.name: South Carolina Code of Laws
code.edition: South Carolina Code of Laws, Title 7 (Elections), as the Legislative Services Agency's site (scstatehouse.gov) prints it on 2026-11-07; the pages carry no 'current through' line, each section shows its own history (latest seen in chapter 17: 2023 Act No. 18)

sc-7-13.citation: S.C. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 13 (Conduct of Elections), Article 19 (General, Special, and Primary Elections Resulting in a Tie): sections 7-13-2210 and 7-13-2220

sc-7-17.citation: S.C. Code Ann. Title 7, Chapter 17 (Canvass of Votes; Certificates and Records of Results): section 7-17-280 (mandatory recounts)

ties.applies_to: any general election or special election, other than a nonpartisan municipal election, that results in a tie vote (S.C. Code 7-13-2210)
ties.steps: if no candidate withdraws, the election officials who conducted the tie election conduct a runoff election to break the tie two weeks after the tie election, under the laws of the State applied mutatis mutandis; a date falling on a legal holiday moves to the same day of the first week after that is not a holiday
ties.who: the election officials who conducted the tied election

sources.quote: If any general election or special election, other than a nonpartisan municipal election, results in a tie vote and no candidate withdraws, the election officials who conducted the tie election shall conduct a runoff election to break the tie two weeks following the tie election.

ties.note: The text says 'any general election or special election' and names no kind of office; it is read as covering U.S. Senate and House, presidential electors, statewide, legislative and (partisan) local offices [inferred for the kinds]. Nonpartisan municipal elections are carved out (see the next rules). No recount before the runoff is required by this article.

ties.applies_to: any primary election, other than a nonpartisan municipal primary election, that results in a tie vote (S.C. Code 7-13-2220)
ties.steps: if no candidate withdraws, the party officials conduct a runoff election to break the tie two weeks after that election, under the laws of the State applied mutatis mutandis; any remaining primary elections required are postponed for two weeks

sources.quote: If any primary election, other than a nonpartisan municipal primary election, results in a tie vote and no candidate withdraws, the party officials shall conduct a runoff election to break the tie two weeks following that election.

ties.applies_to: nonpartisan municipal elections and nonpartisan municipal primary elections
ties.steps: the tie article above excludes them in its own words; what the law says for a tie in a nonpartisan municipal election was not read

sources.quote: If any general election or special election, other than a nonpartisan municipal election, results in a tie vote and no candidate withdraws

ties.note: The municipal election provisions (Title 5 of the Code, and municipal ordinances) were not read; state general law for local offices only, and charters were not read.

ties.applies_to: a constitutional amendment, question or other issue
ties.steps: no provision found saying what a tie vote on a question does
ties.note: Read: Title 7, chapter 13 (searched for tie, by lot, equal number, recount, new election), chapter 17 (read through), chapter 19 and chapter 21 (searched). Article 19 speaks of a tie vote 'and no candidate withdraws', which suggests candidate elections only; whether it reaches a tie on a question was not decided. An absence cannot be confirmed from these chapters alone.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes which were cast for such office
threshold.conditions: the difference between the candidate declared nominated (primary) or elected (general) and any other candidate, or between the candidate who received the least number of votes to qualify for a runoff and a candidate who did not qualify
threshold.in_words: a difference of not more than one percent of the total votes cast for the office, between the declared winner and any other candidate, or at the runoff-qualification line in a primary

recounts.waiver: the other candidate or candidates may waive the recount in writing

sources.quote: Whenever the difference between the number of votes received by a candidate who has been declared nominated for an office in a primary election or who has been declared elected to an office in a general election and the number of votes received by any other candidate or candidate not declared so nominated or elected [...] shall be not more than one percent of the total votes which were cast for such office therein, the committee or board charged by law with canvassing such votes shall order a recount of such votes to be made forthwith unless such other candidate or candidates shall waive a recount in writing.

recounts.note: The text says 'an office' and names no kind; the kinds are a mapping [inferred]. The recount is ordered by 'the committee or board charged by law with canvassing such votes' (the county board of canvassers or the Board of State Canvassers; for a primary the party committee). The quotation is cut at the runoff-qualification clause. A tie is a difference of zero and so falls within the rule; no separate tie-recount rule was found.

threshold.percent_of: the total cast thereon (votes for and against the question)
threshold.conditions: a constitutional amendment, question or other issue; ordered by the Board of State Canvassers
threshold.in_words: a difference between the votes in favor and opposed of not more than one percent of the total cast on the amendment, question or issue

sources.quote: Whenever the difference between the number of votes cast in favor of and opposed to any constitutional amendment, question or other issue is not more than one percent of the total cast thereon, the Board of State Canvassers shall order a recount of such votes to be made forthwith.

unread.what: who pays for a recount, the recount procedure and any recount a candidate may request beyond the one-percent rule; Title 5 (municipal elections); the South Carolina Constitution; State Election Commission regulations
unread.reason: not found in Title 7 chapters 13, 17, 19 and 21 as read; a candidate's remedy found there is a protest or contest of the result on stated grounds (7-17-30, 7-17-260, 7-17-270), which is not a recount request and was not recorded as one. State general law only for local offices.

notes: Read from the General Assembly's Legislative Services Agency site: chapter 13 (whole, searched), chapter 17 (whole), chapter 19 (searched), chapter 21 (read), and the Title 7 chapter index, each fetched once on 2026-11-07.

South Carolina breaks a tie by a runoff two weeks later (not by lot) for general, special and primary elections, unless a candidate withdraws; the mandatory recount threshold is one percent of the votes cast for the office.
